title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
summary: Given a binary search tree and two distinct nodes in it, return their lowest common ancestor.

contractDetails.constraints: 2–100,000 nodes with distinct integer values in [−1,000,000,000, 1,000,000,000]. The input is a BST. Both target nodes are present and distinct.

statement: Given a binary search tree and two distinct nodes in it, return their lowest common ancestor. A node counts as its own ancestor. The examples use node values to identify p and q, and show the returned node's value. The callable returns the actual ancestor node from the input tree.

examples.explanation: The two paths split at node 4.
Node 4 is an ancestor of 7 and itself.
The two nodes are on opposite sides of the root.

constraints: 2–100,000 nodes with distinct integer values in [−1,000,000,000, 1,000,000,000]. The input is a BST. Both target nodes are present and distinct.
hints: Conceptual: The search-tree rule places all lower values on one side and all higher values on the other.
Directional: When both targets are smaller or both are larger than the current node, the ancestor is on that side.
Implementation: Walk down until the targets split across the current node or one target equals it. Return that node.
complexityAnalysis: O(h) time and O(1) auxiliary space for tree height h.
